newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks rally resumes at start of week.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks rally resumes at start of week.

text.p: Jordanian stocks resumed their rally on Saturday with prices at five month highs sparked by persistent healthy outside buying on select blue-chips, dealers said.

The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index climbed 0.98 percent to 149.87 points, its highest level since April, in healthy turnover of 672,056 shares worth 2.04 million dinars ($2.8 million).
Of 51 stocks traded, 25 advanced, 12 fell and 14 were unchanged. None posted year lows.
"New liquidity entered the market and gave the impression to floor traders that investors were coming to the market," said one broker, noting that demand was still focused on blue-chip shares.

Meduim sized portfolios and some foreign buying along with floor trader buying on key stock helped maintain the rebound in prices that has been gathering momentum since end of last month, dealers said.
The market fell at end of June to levels unreached since 1993 on a cash shortage and minimal institutional support.
Arab Bank -- with nearly half of total volume -- was once again the market leader, pulling up other stocks and gaining 3.00 dinars to 247.00 after shares worth 832,110 dinars changed hands.
Another heavily traded bank stock was Housing Bank, which rose 90 fils to 4.97 dinars after half-year profits.

Arab International for Investment and Education, owner of the country's largest private university and relisted on the market after a two month suspension, was again a focus of investor interest with a 40 fils rise to 3.520 dinars on 168,689 dinar turnover.
El Zay Ready Wear, a leading garment producer, saw institutional buying helping push its share up 60 fils to 1.91 dinars.
The Pearl Investable Index -- an independent index of the 45 best-performing shares from the official market -- rose 0.57 percent to 82.50 points, still 13.62 percent down on last year.
